answer.rationale: The 18% mandate + incumbent refusal to reopen terms creates a hard constraint. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor successfully delivered sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing on a prior switch. However, the assembly line at 94% capacity creates real delivery risk if transition falters. Switching to the low-cost vendor alone meets the cost mandate but leaves no second source if onboarding delays occur. memory_c4 shows renegotiation can recover margin, but the incumbent has already refused this cycle. memory_c6 demonstrates multi-year commitments unlock better pricing, but we have only 14 days and the incumbent won't engage. A standard_experiment scale (partial volume trial or phased transition) is inappropriate here given the contract expiration and mandate timeline—we must commit decisively. The switch is justified by prior success (memory_c2) and financial necessity, but delivery risk during transition is the material downside. This decision reduces strategic optionality by consuming our one sourcing slot, leaving us unable to add a second source this cycle.
